name: OS Credential Dumping
summary: Adversaries take credential material out of the operating system.

name: LSASS Memory
summary: Adversaries read credential material out of the LSASS process.

name: Security Account Manager
summary: Adversaries read credential material out of the SAM database.

name: NTDS
summary: Adversaries take the domain database holding every account's hashes.

name: Data from Local System
summary: Adversaries gather data from the system they are on.

name: System Network Configuration Discovery
summary: Adversaries gather network configuration such as addresses and routes.

name: Remote System Discovery
summary: Adversaries list other hosts on the network by address, name or service.

name: Remote Services
summary: Adversaries use valid accounts with remote services to move between hosts.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
summary: Adversaries move between hosts over RDP.

name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
summary: Adversaries move between hosts over SMB administrative shares.

name: SSH
summary: Adversaries move between hosts over SSH.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
summary: Adversaries make a file or its contents hard to discover or to analyze.

name: System Owner/User Discovery
summary: Adversaries identify the user logged in to a system.

name: Masquerading
summary: Adversaries make an artifact look legitimate or benign to a user or a tool.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
summary: Adversaries take data out over the same channel they command the host with.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
summary: Adversaries abuse WMI to run commands and payloads, locally and remotely.

name: System Network Connections Discovery
summary: Adversaries list the network connections a system currently holds.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
summary: Adversaries abuse task scheduling to run code at a set time or on a set event.

name: Cron
summary: Adversaries schedule work with cron.

name: Scheduled Task
summary: Adversaries schedule work with the Windows Task Scheduler.

name: Input Capture
summary: Adversaries capture user input to obtain credentials or other information.

name: Keylogging
summary: Adversaries record keystrokes to capture credentials.

name: Process Discovery
summary: Adversaries list the running processes on a system.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
summary: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters to run commands or binaries.

name: PowerShell
summary: Adversaries run commands and scripts through PowerShell.

name: Windows Command Shell
summary: Adversaries run commands through cmd.exe.

name: Unix Shell
summary: Adversaries run commands through a Unix shell.

name: Visual Basic
summary: Adversaries run code written in Visual Basic, including VBA macros.

name: Python
summary: Adversaries run code through a Python interpreter.

name: JavaScript
summary: Adversaries run code written in JavaScript or JScript.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
summary: Adversaries exploit a software weakness to gain higher-level permissions.

name: Indicator Removal
summary: Adversaries delete or alter artifacts on a system to remove evidence.

name: File Deletion
summary: Adversaries delete files they created or used.

name: Application Layer Protocol
summary: Adversaries hide command and control traffic inside an ordinary protocol.

name: Web Protocols
summary: Command and control traffic is carried over HTTP or HTTPS.

name: DNS
summary: Command and control traffic is carried over DNS.

name: Software Deployment Tools
summary: Adversaries abuse deployment or management software to run commands widely.

name: Valid Accounts
summary: Adversaries obtain and abuse the credentials of an existing account.

name: Default Accounts
summary: Adversaries use accounts that ship with an operating system or a product.

name: Domain Accounts
summary: Adversaries use domain accounts to reach hosts across a network.

name: Local Accounts
summary: Adversaries use accounts local to one host.

name: Cloud Accounts
summary: Adversaries use accounts in a cloud tenant.

name: System Information Discovery
summary: Adversaries gather details about the operating system and hardware.

name: File and Directory Discovery
summary: Adversaries enumerate files and directories to decide what to take next.

name: Account Discovery
summary: Adversaries list the accounts on a system or in a domain.

name: Proxy
summary: Adversaries relay traffic through an intermediate host to hide its origin.

name: Replication Through Removable Media
summary: Adversaries move onto a system by copying malware to removable media.

name: Account Manipulation
summary: Adversaries change an account's settings or credentials to keep access to it.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
summary: Adversaries bring tools or other files onto a compromised system.

name: Brute Force
summary: Adversaries guess passwords or keys when they do not know the credentials.

name: Password Guessing
summary: Adversaries guess passwords for a known account.

name: Password Spraying
summary: Adversaries try one password against many accounts.

name: Modify Registry
summary: Adversaries change the registry to hide configuration or to evade defenses.

name: Screen Capture
summary: Adversaries take screenshots of the victim's desktop.

name: External Remote Services
summary: Adversaries use remote access services such as VPNs to enter or stay in a network.

name: Create Account
summary: Adversaries create an account to keep access to the victim environment.

name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
summary: Adversaries decode or decrypt their own payloads on the victim system.

name: Drive-by Compromise
summary: A user is compromised by visiting a website in the ordinary course of browsing.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
summary: Adversaries exploit a weakness in an internet-facing host or service to gain access.

name: Supply Chain Compromise
summary: Adversaries manipulate a product or a delivery mechanism before it reaches the victim.

name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
summary: Adversaries change software before the victim receives it.

name: Trusted Relationship
summary: Adversaries use a third party with existing access to reach the intended victim.

name: Hardware Additions
summary: Adversaries introduce computer accessories or networking hardware to gain access.

name: Exploitation for Client Execution
summary: Adversaries exploit a weakness in client software to run their own code.

name: User Execution
summary: An adversary relies on a user opening a file or following a link for code to run.

name: Malicious Link
summary: A user is relied on to follow a link.

name: Malicious File
summary: A user is relied on to open a file.

name: Exploitation of Remote Services
summary: Adversaries exploit a service on a remote host to move to it.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution
summary: Adversaries run code through a signed system binary to bypass controls.

name: Data Destruction
summary: Adversaries destroy data and files to interrupt availability.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
summary: Adversaries encrypt data in place to interrupt availability, as ransomware does.

name: Service Stop
summary: Adversaries stop services to deny them to users or to enable other damage.

name: Inhibit System Recovery
summary: Adversaries remove backups and recovery points so a system cannot be restored.

name: Defacement
summary: Adversaries change visible content to intimidate or to make a statement.

name: Resource Hijacking
summary: Adversaries use a victim's compute resources for their own ends.

name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
summary: Adversaries check for an analysis environment and change behavior when they find one.

name: Network Denial of Service
summary: Adversaries exhaust network bandwidth to deny service to users.

name: Endpoint Denial of Service
summary: Adversaries exhaust a host's resources to deny service from it.

name: Server Software Component
summary: Adversaries abuse a server's extensibility to keep access to it.

name: Web Shell
summary: Adversaries install a script on a web server to keep access.

name: Software Discovery
summary: Adversaries list the software and versions installed on a system.

name: Account Access Removal
summary: Adversaries delete or lock accounts to deny access to legitimate users.

name: Create or Modify System Process
summary: Adversaries create or change a system-level process to run malicious payloads.

name: Windows Service
summary: Adversaries create or change a Windows service to run a payload.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
summary: Adversaries configure the system to run code automatically at boot or logon.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
summary: Adversaries add an entry that runs at user logon.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
summary: Adversaries bypass a mechanism that controls elevation to higher privileges.

name: Unsecured Credentials
summary: Adversaries find credentials left in files, registry keys or process memory.

name: Credentials from Password Stores
summary: Adversaries take credentials out of stores such as browsers and keychains.

name: Archive Collected Data
summary: Adversaries compress or encrypt what they have gathered before taking it.

name: Impair Defenses
summary: Adversaries disable or damage security tooling, logging or alerting.

name: Disable or Modify Tools
summary: Adversaries turn off or reconfigure security tooling.

name: Data Manipulation
summary: Adversaries change data to influence a decision or to hide activity.

name: Phishing
summary: Adversaries send messages carrying a malicious attachment or link to gain access.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
summary: A targeted message carries a malicious attachment.

name: Spearphishing Link
summary: A targeted message carries a link to malicious content.

name: Spearphishing via Service
summary: A targeted message arrives through a third-party service.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
summary: Adversaries take data out through a legitimate external web service.

name: System Services
summary: Adversaries abuse system services or daemons to run commands or binaries.

name: Service Execution
summary: Adversaries run a payload through the Windows service control manager.

name: Encrypted Channel
summary: Adversaries encrypt command and control traffic to hide its content.

name: Acquire Infrastructure
summary: Adversaries buy, lease or rent infrastructure to use during targeting.

name: Compromise Infrastructure
summary: Adversaries take over third-party infrastructure to use during targeting.

name: Develop Capabilities
summary: Adversaries build capabilities such as malware, exploits and certificates.

name: Obtain Capabilities
summary: Adversaries buy or steal capabilities rather than developing them.

name: Gather Victim Identity Information
summary: Adversaries gather identity information such as names, email addresses and credentials.

name: Gather Victim Network Information
summary: Adversaries gather network information such as ranges, domains and topology.

name: Active Scanning
summary: Adversaries probe victim infrastructure over the network before compromising it.

name: Stage Capabilities
summary: Adversaries prepare capabilities on infrastructure so they are ready to use.

name: Initial Access
summary: The adversary is trying to get into your network.

name: Execution
summary: The adversary is trying to run malicious code.

name: Persistence
summary: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold.

name: Privilege Escalation
summary: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.

name: Defense Evasion
summary: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected.

name: Credential Access
summary: The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords.

name: Discovery
summary: The adversary is trying to figure out your environment.

name: Lateral Movement
summary: The adversary is trying to move through your environment.

name: Collection
summary: The adversary is trying to gather data of interest to their goal.

name: Exfiltration
summary: The adversary is trying to steal data.

name: Command and Control
summary: The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised systems to control them.

name: Impact
summary: The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt or destroy your systems and data.

name: Resource Development
summary: The adversary is trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.

name: Reconnaissance
summary: The adversary is trying to gather information they can use to plan future operations.
